note.note:
History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe, constant lower central abdominal pain for a few days, worsening; patient rates pain ~8/10.
- Onset/duration/progression: Began a few days ago, progressive worsening over time.
- Location/character: Midline lower abdomen, below the umbilicus; constant.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea (no vomiting), light pink vaginal spotting/bleeding and small vaginal discharge, recent constipation last week now improved.
- Reproductive context: Sexually active; uses contraceptive implant (Implanon) inserted ~1 year ago. Patient had a pregnancy test ~1 month ago (no result recorded). Doctor requested a pregnancy test today.
- Aggravating/alleviating factors: Pain worsening; no clear alleviating factors reported.
- Red flags denied/documented negative symptoms: No fever reported, no shortness of breath, no shoulder-tip pain, no syncope/fainting, no problems with passing urine noted, able to perform usual activities.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: None reported.
- Surgical history: No prior operations.
- Obstetric/gynecologic history: No previous pregnancies.
- Medications: Contraceptive implant — Implanon (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Amoxicillin allergy reported.
- Social: Age 23, school teacher, lives with husband and his family. Denies recreational drugs. Alcohol use unclear (patient response unclear).

Physical Examination:
- Vital signs: Not recorded.
- Abdominal findings: No formal abdominal or pelvic examination documented in the transcript.
- Reported/observed exam items: Patient agreed to face-to-face examination for abdominal/pelvic assessment.
- Relevant negatives (documented): No vomiting, no feverish feeling, no difficulty breathing, no urinary symptoms, no fainting.
- Mental status/orientation: Not recorded.

Impression:
- One-line clinical impression: Acute severe lower central abdominal pain in a reproductive-age woman with light vaginal bleeding — urgent face-to-face assessment required to exclude acute gynecologic causes (e.g., adnexal torsion, ectopic pregnancy, ruptured ovarian cyst).
- DDx consistent with transcript (top 2–3 plausible diagnoses with brief justifications):
  1. Ovarian/adnexal torsion — high concern: severe, constant pelvic pain with nausea and progressive course fits torsion (transcript consistent).
  2. Ectopic pregnancy — medium concern: vaginal bleeding and pelvic pain in sexually active woman; pregnancy test now required (transcript supports checking pregnancy).
  3. Ruptured or hemorrhagic ovarian cyst — medium concern: can present with acute pelvic pain and spotting (consistent with transcript).

Management Plan:
- Immediate/advised actions from the encounter:
  - Arrange face-to-face clinic appointment for formal abdominal and pelvic examination — patient instructed to call the support line to book this.
  - Patient to perform a pregnancy test today; instructed to report back if positive.
  - Advise earlier/urgent review if symptoms significantly worsen (increasing pain), inability to keep fluids down, heavy vaginal bleeding, syncope, or other acute deterioration.
- Additional planning (as discussed/supported by transcript context):
  - Clinical assessment in person to guide further investigations and management; further steps to be decided after examination.
- No medications or procedures were prescribed during this consultation.

Patient Summary:
- A 23-year-old woman with a one-year Implanon contraceptive implant presents with several days of progressively worsening, severe central lower abdominal pain (8/10), associated with nausea and light vaginal spotting. A face-to-face abdominal/pelvic examination and an immediate pregnancy test were arranged/ requested; urgent review advised if pain or other symptoms worsen.

Key Takeaways:
- Call the support line to arrange a face-to-face clinic appointment for abdominal/pelvic examination.
- Do a pregnancy test today and contact the service immediately if it is positive.
- Return or seek urgent care sooner if pain markedly worsens, cannot tolerate fluids, or if heavy bleeding or fainting occurs.

Next Steps:
- Patient to perform pregnancy test today and phone results.
- Patient to contact support line to book an in-person abdominal/pelvic examination promptly.
- If clinical findings on examination suggest, further investigations (e.g., urgent gynecologic review/imaging) will be arranged at the face-to-face visit.

- Missing/expected elements not present in transcript:
  - Vital signs (HR, BP, temperature, RR) not recorded.
  - No physical exam findings documented (abdominal/pelvic exam not performed).
  - No pregnancy test result recorded (patient reports one done ~1 month ago; current test pending).
  - No laboratory or imaging results documented.
  - Medication list incomplete for non-contraceptive meds (none reported) — full medication reconciliation not available.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None significant; DDx aligns with transcript findings. (Note: timing of recent sexual intercourse and timing wording had minor confusion in transcript — DDx correctly flags need for up-to-date pregnancy testing.)
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Overall intelligible; occasional unclear timing statements and brief inaudible moments.
